div.head:
287. Robert Southey to Grosvenor Charles Bedford, 5 February 1798Address: G. C. Bedford Esqr. / Exchequer
Endorsement: 5 Feby 1798
MS: Bodleian Library, MS Eng. Lett. c. 23. ALS; 2p.
Unpublished.
div.p: Will you fix an early day for dining at Grays Inn. We leave town next week, & as I have seen you so frequently since we have resided here, I shall of course feel much at the seperation. let me not forget to thank you for Musæus.Grosvenor Charles Bedford’s translation of Musaeus (fl. c. early 6th century), The Loves of Hero and Leander (1797).

Edith has been very unwell – I hope better air, & regular exercise will restore her health. I suppose Grosvenor, in about a fortnight we shall be very intimate again – as we shall be a hundred miles asunder.

closer.salute: I wish to keep the term this week.

postscript.p: [a sketch of a woman’s head and shoulders in an unknown hand, possibly Southey’s, is on fol 1 v]
